For a function [MATH: f(x,y),] the double integral of [MATH: f] over a rectangular region [MATH: R] is the unique number [MATH: I] (if it exists) such that

[MATH: L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P)]

over all partitions [MATH: P] of [MATH: R,] where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

[MATH: L(f, P)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)m_{ij}Δx_{i}Δy_{j}; U(f, P)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)M_{ij}Δx_{i}Δy_{j}]

and [MATH: m_{ij}] and [MATH: M_{ij}] are the minimum and maximum values of [MATH: f] respectively in each subregion [MATH: R_{ij}.]

We need to compute [MATH: U(f,P).]

Notice that for all subregions [MATH: R_{ij},] we have that

  • [MATH: f(x,y) = 12-x-y] decreases as [MATH: x] increases, and

  • [MATH: f(x,y) = 12-x-y] decreases as [MATH: y] increases.

As a result, the maximum value of [MATH: f] in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible [MATH: x] and the smallest possible [MATH: y.] This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion. Therefore,

[MATH: M_{ij} = f(x_{i-1}, y_{j-1}) = 12-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1}]

and the upper Riemann sum is given by

[MATH: U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (12-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j.]

Item 2 — Example: Applying the Definition of the Double Integral in Terms of Lower and Upper Riemann Sums

Example Prompt:
Let [MATH: R = [0,1]\times [1,2]] be a region in the [MATH: xy]-plane, and let [MATH: f(x,y) = 12-x-y.] Further, let

[MATH: \displaystyle I = \iint\limits_{R} f(x,y)\,\textrm dA]

be the unique number such that over all rectangular partitions [MATH: P] of [MATH: R,] we have
[MATH: L(f,P)\:\leq I \:\leq U(f,P),]
where [MATH: L(f,P)] and [MATH: U(f,P)] are the corresponding lower and upper Riemann sums. Write down the upper Riemann sum [MATH: U(f,P).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
For a function [MATH: f(x,y),] the double integral of [MATH: f] over a rectangular region [MATH: R] is the unique number [MATH: I] (if it exists) such that

[MATH: L(f,P) \leq I \leq U(f,P)]

over all partitions [MATH: P] of [MATH: R,] where the lower and upper sums respectively are given by

[MATH: L(f, P)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)m_{ij}Δx_{i}Δy_{j}; U(f, P)|= ∑_(i = 1)^(m)∑_(j = 1)^(n)M_{ij}Δx_{i}Δy_{j}]

and [MATH: m_{ij}] and [MATH: M_{ij}] are the minimum and maximum values of [MATH: f] respectively in each subregion [MATH: R_{ij}.]

We need to compute [MATH: U(f,P).]

Notice that for all subregions [MATH: R_{ij},] we have that

- [MATH: f(x,y) = 12-x-y] decreases as [MATH: x] increases, and
- [MATH: f(x,y) = 12-x-y] decreases as [MATH: y] increases.

As a result, the maximum value of [MATH: f] in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible [MATH: x] and the smallest possible [MATH: y.] This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion. Therefore,

[MATH: M_{ij} = f(x_{i-1}, y_{j-1}) = 12-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1}]

and the upper Riemann sum is given by

[MATH: U(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n (12-x_{i-1}-y_{j-1})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j.]
